chunks: Jabir ibn Yazid said: I came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, the differences among the Shia in their doctrines have caused me pain.' He said: 'O Jabir, did I not acquaint you with the meaning of their differences, from where they differed and from which direction they separated?' I said: 'Yes, O son of the Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Do not differ when they differ, O Jabir. The one who denies the Master of the Age is like the one who denied the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) in his days. O Jabir, listen and retain.' I said: 'Whenever you wish.' He said: 'Listen, retain, and convey wherever your mount takes you — that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) delivered a sermon to the people in Medina seven days after the passing of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and that was when he had finished collecting and compiling the Quran. And he said:

Praise be to Allah Who prevented imaginations from attaining anything except His existence, and veiled the intellects from conceiving His essence due to their transcendence above similarity and likeness. He is the One in Whose essence there is no variation, nor division into numerical parts in His perfection. He is distinct from things — not by being in different places — and He is present within them — not by way of mingling. He knows them — not by means of an instrument without which knowledge cannot exist. And there is not between Him and His known any other knowledge — He is the Knowing by Himself. If it is said He was, it is interpreted as the eternity of existence; if it is said He never ceases, it is interpreted as the negation of non-existence. Glorified and exalted is He above the words of those who worship other than Him and take a god other than Him — a great exaltation. We praise Him with a praise that He accepted from His creation and made obligatory upon Himself. I testify that there is no god but Allah alone, with no associate for Him, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His messenger — two testimonies that elevate the word and multiply the deed. Light is the scale from which they are raised, and heavy is the scale on which they are placed. By them is the attainment of Paradise and the salvation from Fire and the passage over the Bridge. By the testimony you enter Paradise, and by prayer you attain mercy. Send blessings frequently upon your Prophet — for indeed Allah and His angels bless the Prophet: O you who believe...

O those who believe, send blessings upon him and salute him with worthy salutations. May Allah bless him, his family, and salute them with perfect salutation. O you people! There is no honor higher than Islam, no nobility more precious than piety, no stronghold more secure than scrupulousness, no intercessor more successful than repentance, no garment more beautiful than wellbeing, no shield more protective than safety, no wealth more effective than contentment, no virtue more beneficial than knowledge, no worship like contemplation, no lord more praiseworthy than Allah, no companion better than good character, no heritage more esteemed than manners, no guide more reliable than guidance, no trade more profitable than righteous deeds, no provision better than God-consciousness, no spokesman more eloquent than silence at the right time, no determination without awareness, and no knowledge without certainty. O you people! No good is there in silence about wisdom, nor in speaking with ignorance.

O you people! Whoever examines the fault of his own self is occupied from the faults of others. Whoever is satisfied with Allah's provision does not grieve over what is in another's hand. Whoever draws the sword of transgression will be killed by it. Whoever digs a pit for his brother falls into it. Whoever tears the veil of another's privacy will have his own privacy exposed. Whoever forgets his own sins considers the sins of others great. Whoever relies on good opinion of people will be let down. Whoever is proud of his lineage will fall short. Whoever is arrogant toward his Lord, Allah will humiliate him. Whoever seeks elevation through injustice, Allah will lower him. Whoever does not control his tongue will regret. Whoever does not have knowledge will be ignorant. Whoever does not exercise patience will not have forbearance. Whoever does not hold back will not have reason. Whoever is not humble will be humiliated. Whoever wastes time loses the chance. Whoever has bad character punishes himself. The example of the envious one is that of fire consuming itself.

There is no good in silence about wisdom, just as there is no good in speaking with ignorance. Know, O you people, that whoever does not control his tongue will regret, whoever does not know will be ignorant, whoever does not exercise forbearance will have no clemency, whoever does not restrain himself will have no reason, whoever does not learn will be dishonored, whoever does not take lessons from experiences loses insight, whoever does not reflect before speaking will err, whoever does not have steadfastness will tire, whoever has no foresight will be surprised by events. Being deceived by the present life is ignorance, and being preoccupied by it is heedlessness. The scholar knows that the world is a passage, so he does not settle in it and does not build upon it. The people of the world are as travelers who spend a night and move on in the morning. Have gratitude for blessings lest they depart, and be patient in trials lest they intensify. Submit to God's decree and do not resent it, for contentment is wisdom and resentment exhausts the soul without benefit.

Anger — and if made happy by approval he forgets vigilance; and if fear reaches him, apprehension occupies him; and if security expands for him, pride seizes him; [and in another version: pride takes him]; and if a blessing is renewed for him, pride takes him; and if he gains wealth, opulence makes him arrogant; and if affliction strikes him, impatience reveals him. The state of people oscillates between these conditions — dominated by passions in most states. Happy is the one who guards himself against all these. The lowly person is dominated by his ego. The noble one subdues his ego. The intelligent person is he who masters his desires, and works for what is after death. The foolish one follows his whims and hopes in Allah while falling short. Beware of the company of the corrupt, for corruption spreads. Keep company with the righteous and benefiting from them is near. The miser's wealth does not benefit him in life, nor does it save him after death.

Minds restrain and forbid, and in experiences there is a newly gained knowledge, and consideration leads to righteousness. Sufficient as discipline for yourself is what you dislike for others. Upon you is owed to your believing brother what he owes to you. Whoever relied solely on his own opinion has risked, and deliberation before action protects from regret. Know that the people of every age and time alternate between a blessing that is exhausted and a calamity that endures. So they continue this way until Allah sends a time that pleases Him and the people of it. Whoever performs an act of kindness and then mentions it has disgraced himself. Beware of lying, for it leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. The righteous do not lie. The truthful is upon a path, and the liar is upon a slippery ground. The intelligent person considers the consequence. Whoever discloses your secret takes your honor. Keep your secret hidden from your enemy and from your friend; for perhaps your friend will become your enemy. Use gentleness with those who are harsh to you, for perhaps they will come to know. Seek the good from those of nobility. Woven around every neck is a necklace of deeds.

The softness of speech, and of worship is manifestation of the tongue and spreading of peace. Beware of deception, for it is from the character of the ignoble. Not every seeker attains, and not every absent one returns. Do not desire one who has lost interest in you. Perhaps a distant one is closer than a near one. Ask about the companion before the road. Do not rush in building a friendship until you test the companion. Be wary of the companion of vile character. Do not give counsel in what is not asked of you, for the person of judgment does not do that. Guard your secret from your enemy and from your friend; for perhaps your friend will become your enemy. Take care of your wealth and your religion. Do not boast of an ancestry that is weak in deeds, for deeds elevate people, not lineages. The lineage of every virtuous person is his good deeds. Beware of resentment, for it exhausts the soul without benefit. The generous person is close in spirit even if distant in person, and the miser is far even if near in body.

His promise is true, and Allah will never break His promise. Beware, indeed al-Waseela is on the steps of Paradise, at the peak of the pinnacles of nearness, and the ultimate end of wishes. It has a thousand steps, the distance between each step and the next being the gallop of a noble horse for a hundred years. And it is between two gates of Paradise — the gate of mercy and the gate of repentance — and on its right is the station of the Prophet and on its left is the station of Abraham, and behind it is the House of Praise filled with the light of the Lord, exalted be He. Whoever longs for al-Waseela among those who submit among the believing men and women, let them then hasten to its cause by supplication and nearness to it. One who enters Paradise with supplication toward al-Waseela does not move except that he sees it and those who dwell in it from the people of nearness — may Allah have mercy on them — and they are the chosen ones among the servants, who do not ask Allah for anything without it being given to them, and they do not intercede except by His permission.

Turning away from Allah, His Prophet, His path, and the signs of the ages — be certain of the blackening of your faces and the wrath of your Lord as recompense for what you used to do. And there is not a messenger who passed, nor a prophet who preceded, except that he had informed his community of the messenger coming after him, and warned them of his enemies. And Allah did not cease sending prophets and messengers informing communities of what would come to be, until the chain ended with Muhammad — the Seal of Prophets — may Allah bless him and his family, and the final of messengers. After him there is no prophet, and there is no knowledge of the unseen except from Allah's information. O people, I informed you today of what you will find tomorrow when you stand before your Lord to be judged. Whoever harmed my household has harmed me, and whoever caused pain to me has caused pain to Allah. Allah has guided you through our Ahlul Bayt and shown you the path of truth and falsehood.

Like Aaron from Moses, except that there is no prophet after me. The believers understood from Allah what the Messenger spoke when they recognized me — that I am not his brother through his father and mother as Aaron was Moses' brother through his father and mother, and I was not a prophet, implying prophethood. But that was from Allah Who revealed to His Messenger and He informed of it and appointed it for me as Imamate and vicegerency. So whoever believes in it will be guided. By it you will be guided to the truth. He who does not believe in it has turned from the path. And Allah supported me with it by the revelation and by the declaration at Ghadir Khumm. The Prophet said: 'Whoever I am his master, Ali is his master. O Allah, befriend those who befriend him, and be hostile to those who are hostile to him, and help those who help him, and forsake those who forsake him.' Thus the truth became clear. Know that the most knowledgeable of you after me is the Imam after me. And he is established by the covenant of Allah and His Messenger. And after him is the covenant continuing until the Day of Judgment.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic called His Prophet and raised him to Himself. No sooner had that happened — it was like a glance from a beat or a flash from lightning — they turned on their heels and reversed course and sought vengeance and brought forth armies and raised the banner of people of corruption. And they mounted upon the backs of people of religion, and plundered the inheritance of the Prophets. So know that you will indeed be recompensed on the Day of Resurrection for what you sent forth from deeds, and that the most wronged among you is the most deserving of a just decision. Whoever has a grievance, let him bring it forward, and be well-acquainted with what the Book says, and what the Sunna commands, and what reason and knowledge demand. The argument of Allah upon His servants is the Quran, and after it the Prophet, and after him the Commander of the Faithful, and after him the Imams who are guides and the guided. They are the successors in this earth established by Allah's command and sovereignty, and witnesses for His servants. The one who follows them is guided, and the one who opposes them is misguided.
ai.seo_question: What is the Sermon of the Means (Khutbat al-Waseela) by Imam Ali, transmitted through Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith presents the 'Sermon of the Means' (Khutbat al-Waseela), a sweeping theological and ethical address delivered by Imam Ali (AS) in Medina seven days after the Prophet's death, transmitted through Imam al-Baqir (AS) to Jabir ibn Yazid. The sermon opens with profound affirmations of divine transcendence and tawhid, followed by extensive wisdom teachings on ethics, virtues, and character, then describes the celestial station of al-Waseela in Paradise, and culminates in a declaration of Imam Ali's wilaya and imamate backed by Quranic evidence, concluding with historical accounts of deviation and its consequences.
word_analysis: the Age/Era (the Imam of the time)
